definition: A human memory B cell that expresses Fc receptor-like protein 4 (FCRL4) and Fc receptor-like protein 5 (FCRL5) together with integrin alpha-X (CD11c), and is characteristically CD27-negative, CD21-low, CD38-negative, IgM-negative, and IgD-negative, with class-switched (IgG or IgA) somatically mutated B cell receptors (PMID:16157685). This cell resides in sub-epithelial regions of mucosa-associated lymphoid tissues, particularly the crypt epithelium and perifollicular zones of the palatine tonsil, and is largely absent from blood, bone marrow, and spleen (PMID:18625746). It is hyporesponsive to B cell receptor ligation but retains the capacity to respond to CD40 signals and cytokines, and its antibody repertoire is enriched for commensal microbial reactivity (PMID:29703863, PMID:28756897). FCRL4-positive memory B cells occur throughout mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (tonsil, Peyer's patches, intestinal lymphoid tissue, mesenteric lymph nodes) and are not restricted to the tonsil (PMID:18625746). All three defining markers are documented at the protein level (cell-surface, by antibody/flow cytometry), not merely as transcripts: FCRL4 (PMID:16157685), CD11c (PMID:24431391), and FCRL5 (PMID:34745084). FCRL4 and FCRL5 belong to the Fc receptor-like family, which lacks clean 1:1 mouse orthologs, so this marker-defined cell type is specified as human.

logical_axioms.notes: Resides within the mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue of secondary lymphoid organs (broad ASTA search: not tonsil-restricted); the source atlas sampled human palatine tonsil.
FCRL4 surface protein confirmed by monoclonal-antibody flow cytometry (PMID:16157685).
FCRL5 surface protein confirmed by flow cytometry (PMID:34745084).
CD11c (integrin alpha-X) surface protein confirmed by flow cytometry (PMID:24431391).
These cells reside at mucosal surfaces and their antibody repertoire is biased towards commensal microbial antigens, consistent with participation in mucosal immune homeostasis.

Human-specific cell type: FCRL4/FCRL5 belong to the FCRL family, which lacks clean 1:1 mouse orthologs, so the term is restricted to Homo sapiens (CL '…, human' pattern; parent CL:0000787 remains species-neutral).

justification: No CL term exists for FCRL4-positive atypical/tissue-based memory B cells or any CD27-negative class-switched memory B cell subset. The nearest candidate, CL:0000972 ('class switched memory B cell'), explicitly requires CD27-positive surface expression in its definition, which directly contradicts the defining CD27-negative phenotype of FCRL4+ cells. Although FCRL4/5+ cells are class-switched (IgG/IgA), assigning CL:0000972 as parent would misrepresent a core biological feature. CL:0000787 ('memory B cell') is the correct direct parent: FCRL4/5+ cells satisfy core memory B cell criteria (antigen-experienced, long-lived, high-affinity somatically mutated Ig, CD19-positive, CD20-high, CD138-negative) but the existing term does not capture the FCRL4/FCRL5 defining surface markers, CD27-negativity, tissue restriction to sub-epithelial mucosal lymphoid niches, CD21-low phenotype, or the hyporesponsive functional programme that distinguishes this population from classical memory B cells. Note: a CD27-negative class-switched memory B cell intermediate term placed between CL:0000787 and this proposed term may also be warranted, and is flagged for CL editor consideration. Note: in the King et al. atlas itself detection is transcript/chromatin-level (scRNA/scATAC); protein evidence derives from the cited literature.] [Revised 2026-07-28: de-anchored from palatine tonsil. A broad ASTA tissue-distribution search established this is a general population of secondary lymphoid organs / MALT rather than a palatine-tonsil-specific type; the tonsil is merely the tissue sampled by the atlas. Label and location axiom generalised accordingly (location → mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue, UBERON:0001961). [Revised 2026-07-28: made HUMAN-SPECIFIC per curator decision. The defining FCRL4/FCRL5 markers are members of the Fc receptor-like family that lack clean 1:1 mouse orthologs, so the generic 'gene or 1:1 ortholog' PR semantics are inappropriate here. Marker axioms switched to human PR terms (FCRL4 PR:Q96PJ5, FCRL5 PR:Q96RD9, CD11c PR:P20702) and an 'only in taxon' Homo sapiens (NCBITaxon:9606) restriction added; parent CL:0000787 (memory B cell) kept species-neutral. ## New term request: FCRL4-positive memory B cell, human

**Proposed label:** FCRL4-positive memory B cell, human

**Definition:** A human memory B cell that expresses Fc receptor-like protein 4 (FCRL4) and Fc receptor-like protein 5 (FCRL5) together with integrin alpha-X (CD11c), and is characteristically CD27-negative, CD21-low, CD38-negative, IgM-negative, and IgD-negative, with class-switched (IgG or IgA) somatically mutated B cell receptors (PMID:16157685). This cell resides in sub-epithelial regions of mucosa-associated lymphoid tissues, particularly the crypt epithelium and perifollicular zones of the palatine tonsil, and is largely absent from blood, bone marrow, and spleen (PMID:18625746). It is hyporesponsive to B cell receptor ligation but retains the capacity to respond to CD40 signals and cytokines, and its antibody repertoire is enriched for commensal microbial reactivity (PMID:29703863, PMID:28756897). FCRL4-positive memory B cells occur throughout mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (tonsil, Peyer's patches, intestinal lymphoid tissue, mesenteric lymph nodes) and are not restricted to the tonsil (PMID:18625746). All three defining markers are documented at the protein level (cell-surface, by antibody/flow cytometry), not merely as transcripts: FCRL4 (PMID:16157685), CD11c (PMID:24431391), and FCRL5 (PMID:34745084). FCRL4 and FCRL5 belong to the Fc receptor-like family, which lacks clean 1:1 mouse orthologs, so this marker-defined cell type is specified as human.

**Parent (is_a):** memory B cell (CL:0000787)

**Anatomical location:** mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (UBERON:0001961)

**Logical axioms:**
- `part of` (BFO:0000050) some **mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue** (UBERON:0001961) — Resides within the mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue of secondary lymphoid organs (broad ASTA search: not tonsil-restricted); the source atlas sampled human palatine tonsil.
- `has plasma membrane part` (RO:0002104) some **Fc receptor-like protein 4 (human)** (PR:Q96PJ5) — FCRL4 surface protein confirmed by monoclonal-antibody flow cytometry (PMID:16157685).
- `has plasma membrane part` (RO:0002104) some **Fc receptor-like protein 5 (human)** (PR:Q96RD9) — FCRL5 surface protein confirmed by flow cytometry (PMID:34745084).
- `has plasma membrane part` (RO:0002104) some **integrin alpha-X (human)** (PR:P20702) — CD11c (integrin alpha-X) surface protein confirmed by flow cytometry (PMID:24431391).
- `capable of part of` (RO:0002216) some **mucosal immune response** (GO:0002385) — These cells reside at mucosal surfaces and their antibody repertoire is biased towards commensal microbial antigens, consistent with participation in mucosal immune homeostasis.
- `only in taxon` (RO:0002160) some **Homo sapiens** (NCBITaxon:9606) — Human-specific cell type: FCRL4/FCRL5 belong to the FCRL family, which lacks clean 1:1 mouse orthologs, so the term is restricted to Homo sapiens (CL '…, human' pattern; parent CL:0000787 remains species-neutral).

**Synonyms:**
- atypical memory B cell (related)
- tissue-based memory B cell (related)
- tissue-like memory B cell (related)
- FCRL4/5-positive memory B cell (exact)
- FcRH4-positive memory B cell (exact)
- CD21-low atypical memory B cell (narrow)

**References:**
- Ehrhardt et al. (2005). DOI: 10.1084/jem.20050879 ; PMID:16157685 — Original description of FCRL4+ (FcRH4+) tissue-based memory B cell population in human tonsil; defining markers FCRL4, CD11c, CD27-negativity, class-switched BCR; sub-epithelial localisation.
- Ehrhardt et al. (2008). DOI: 10.1084/jem.20072682 ; PMID:18625746 — Anatomical distribution: crypt epithelium and perifollicular regions of palatine tonsil, intestinal lymphoid tissues, mesenteric lymph nodes; absence from blood, bone marrow, spleen.
- Karnell et al. (2017). DOI: 10.1016/j.cellimm.2017.05.008 ; PMID:28756897 — Functional characterisation: hyporesponsiveness to BCR ligation, retained response to CD40/cytokine signals; class-switched (90% IgG/IgA) BCR; synonym 'tissue-like memory B cell'.
- Liu et al. (2018). DOI: 10.4049/jimmunol.1701549 ; PMID:29703863 — FCRL4 as low-affinity IgA receptor with immunoregulatory potential; antibody repertoire enriched for commensal microbial reactivity.
- Jourdan et al. (2017). DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0179793 ; PMID:28636654 — Characterisation of FCRL4+ B cells including reduced plasma cell differentiation potential; sub-epithelial localisation in lymphoid tissues.
- Gjertsson et al. (2022). DOI: 10.1093/cei/uxac103 ; PMID:36380692 — Consensus surface phenotype CD27-negative, IgD-negative, CD38-negative, CD11c-positive, FCRL4-positive; ~10% of tonsillar B cells, <0.5% in peripheral blood/bone marrow/spleen.
- King et al. (2021). DOI: 10.1126/sciimmunol.abh3768 ; PMID:34623901 — Atlas source paper — FCRL4/5+ label in Azimuth human_tonsil_v2 reference dataset.

**Justification:** No CL term exists for FCRL4-positive atypical/tissue-based memory B cells or any CD27-negative class-switched memory B cell subset. The nearest candidate, CL:0000972 ('class switched memory B cell'), explicitly requires CD27-positive surface expression in its definition, which directly contradicts the defining CD27-negative phenotype of FCRL4+ cells. Note: in the King et al. atlas itself detection is transcript/chromatin-level (scRNA/scATAC); protein evidence derives from the cited literature.] [Revised 2026-07-28: de-anchored from palatine tonsil.
